title: Lane previews are owned by their lane and stopped by pid
trigger: 2026-10-24: five astro preview processes (ports 3000, 3100, 3200, 3300, 3400) were left orphaned (ppid 1) by finished lanes. One pkill -f on the preview command line matched the invoking shell's own command line and killed it (exit 144), losing a screenshot run. One lane could not stop its own preview and handed the kill to the coordinator.
root_cause: Lanes started previews without recording who owned them, and stopped processes by a command-line substring that also appears in the caller's own command line. Nothing tied a preview's lifetime to the lane that started it.
rule: A lane starts its preview on a lane-unique port, records the pid, and stops exactly that pid before hand-back; match processes by $2 ~ /node$/ on `ps -eo pid,args` output and never by a substring that appears in the caller's own command line.
reuse_boundary: Local development lanes only. CI runs a fresh runner per job. Applies to any project that runs a local preview server per lane. It never authorises killing a process the lane did not start.

guard.judgment_only_reason: A process-level guard (a wrapper that owns and reaps previews) would live in scripts/, which is a protected path and out of this change. The failure is also lane behaviour at hand-back, not repository content a test can inspect. The adjacent failure, a busy port 3000, is already refused by reuseExistingServer: false (LSN-marketing-002); a lane-unique port plus recorded pid is a judgment-level checklist.
